claims.statement: The Together editorial case-study shell and the Spade product-brand layer are distinct sources of visual rules.
Sparse explanatory regions alternate with dense proof-bearing regions across both source presentations.
Data labels are spatially attached to an object, transaction or outcome rather than used as free decoration.
A proof region establishes one primary visual protagonist and subordinates annotations around it.
Boundaries communicate measurement and instrumentation, but their exact rails and corner geometry are source-specific.
The centered title/object/CTA sequence and lateral measurement rails form a source-specific Hero topology.
Contour object, transaction chip, green family, cut boundaries and monospace labels become signature-like when combined.
Evidence-first hierarchy, semantic attachment and controlled signal count remain useful after palette, object, typography and topology change.
